title: Days Since You Last LAUGHED 🤫
premise: In a town where a number over every head counts the days since you last laughed, my stressed little brother has crammed for finals in a silent domed reading room until his number says forty, and a person printed in reverse, with an upside-down grin and no number at all, moves a table nearer each time someone swallows a laugh.
twist: The thing is made of every laugh swallowed under the dome, so the silence feeds it and it goes to whoever holds in the most; one laugh rolls a number back to zero, so I break the room's rule and tell our dumbest old joke out loud, my brother cracks, the whole room laughs, and it comes apart.
world: A sunny round public reading room under a glass dome of square panes, with oak tables, green-and-brass lamps on one closing timer, tall stacks of plain books and a window in the west wall, plus a bright street and a front doorstep.
